text.title: AI Prompt Patterns for Test Ideation Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether the unit has a deterministic oracle, whether it has enough branches and invariants to repay ideation, and whether a property-based suite already covers them — to full ideation, property extension, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the unit have a deterministic oracle — a checkable relation between input and output — rather than "looks right" output such as rendering fidelity or model quality?

conclusion.verdict: skip; route to golden-file or human-review testing — generated assertions would encode one arbitrary snapshot as truth

branch.question: Does the unit carry at least one branch or stated invariant, as opposed to a one-line accessor, a pure data class, or a delegation?

conclusion.verdict: skip; on a getter the mutation run costs more than reading the code it examines

branch.question: Is a property-based suite (Hypothesis, fast-check, QuickCheck) already asserting this unit's invariants?

conclusion.verdict: do not restart ideation; extend the existing properties with any missing relation — round-trip, idempotence, order-invariance, conservation
apply the full methodology: spec-only boundary prompt, relational oracles, then gate acceptance on a mutation run over the target module
